source_row.extraction_instructions: Cloudflare-protected dedicated flagship microsite (not a listing of many events) — self.browser.navigate() clears the challenge via context rotation. list_shells_override() reads /about/future-meetings' Year|Date|Location table and emits ONE shell for whichever year is soonest-upcoming (title 'ARVO Annual Meeting <year>', booking_url = /registration). extract_detail() then walks /registration (two plain multi-column fee tables: core Rates + CME Rates, USD), /about (accordions for venue address + abstract deadline, server-rendered but display:none), and /abstracts (fallback deadline parse). All fees stored with currency='USD'.

concerns: Only ONE shell is ever emitted (the next Annual Meeting) — this is a dedicated flagship microsite with no other dated events under arvo.org/annual-meeting/. If ARVO later adds other meeting types on this domain, they will not be picked up without extending list_shells_override().

cpd_points is always None — ARVO states the Meeting is CME-accredited (AMA PRA Category 1 Credit) but never publishes a numeric credit/hour count on the public pages. cpd_accredited=True is set instead.

Venue/abstract-deadline regexes match the CURRENT (2026-09-29) accordion wording ('X is located at Y', 'Abstract submission deadline') and the exact div class 'accordion-content' from the Alpine.js-driven About page. If ARVO changes that template, these fields will silently return None — self-heals via the existing PLAYBOOK.md rule (event_format IS NULL or venue/city IS NULL re-triggers a re-fetch next scrape) rather than locking in stale data.

Two harness runs produced identical results (1 shell, 21 pricing tiers) but --force-fallback wasn't meaningfully exercisable: this extractor is browser-first throughout (self.browser.navigate() for every page, never httpx/fetch_html), matching the wave 1c/1d addenda, so http_fetch's httpx-403 patch has no effect on it either way.

Registration page occasionally needs a Cloudflare context rotation that fails on the FIRST attempt within the same browser session as the future-meetings fetch (observed once during development — browser.py warned 'not cleared by either browser profile' and silently kept the stale future-meetings page). Guarded in extract_detail() by verifying the handed-in page's URL contains '/registration' AND its HTML contains 'Registration Rates' before trusting it, else re-fetching via a fresh navigate(); did not recur on either logged harness run but is a live possibility on a slower/busier scrape.
